result.decision_rationale:
The focused gate passed on the candidate. It confirms that the controller releases an unreachable target before first dispatch in the reported round-9 case. An installed wrapper can still start moving before that check runs, and an ineligible retained target can still veto a fresh proposal. The check also uses stale weapon reach and can mask an actual target invalidation. The queued invalidation output is correct, but its regression assertion still accepts an extra rejection code.

## Continuation for Claude

The operator ledger records round 10 as PR-1’s final allocated review. Any further formal round requires owner authorization. If work resumes, use the current rider action range and sight for the retained target wherever the automatic order can authorize movement, delivery, or refusal of a replacement proposal. Give the exact unreleased wrapper’s target invalidation precedence over either geometry-only retirement. Preserve native completion of released strikes, player orders, turn-based follow-through and ordinary advance toward reachable enemies.

Exercise the affected event orderings through the existing attack-path harness. Record wrapper and move submissions, first delivery, spending, and the exact terminal code list. Bind the required focused gate to the corrected candidate. Native play and packaging remain outside this checkpoint.

findings.actual: AutomaticTargetLeftNativeAdmission is called only by TryRetireStockIntent. The installed wrapper checks group memory and pair-wide movement permission. Both still pass for this mobile pair. TickPreStartApproach can therefore call BeginPreStartMove and submit a mount move toward B before the controller retires it.
findings.blocking_rationale: The horse can receive a movement order toward an enemy the native brain currently excludes. Later cancellation cannot undo movement already taken.
findings.expected: The unreleased wrapper ends before issuing or adopting movement toward B.
findings.requested_correction: Make current target-specific admission available to the automatic wrapper at its pre-start, approach and first-delivery boundaries. Preserve exact carrier cleanup and native handling after delivery.
findings.requested_evidence: Install the automatic wrapper while B is legal, keep native start waiting, move B out of range, then tick the wrapper before the controller. Record zero new move submissions, displacement and spending. Retain the reachable-target control.
findings.title: An installed automatic wrapper can approach an unreachable target before the controller rechecks it
findings.trigger: The rider’s automatic wrapper is in its native Standard slot for an in-range, perceived B marked unreachable. B moves outside action range before the wrapper’s next native approach tick, which runs before the controller drive.

findings.actual: The new branch sets the reason to 'automatic target outside native admission'. Only HoldOutOfReach enters the TargetInvalidNow precedence check. The drive and queue promotion therefore retire the wrapper as Cancelled and produce CommandCancelled. The wrapper’s own tick checks target validity first and produces TargetInvalid.
findings.blocking_rationale: The same unconscious target produces different terminal feedback and rejection codes depending on which observer runs first.
findings.expected: All three observers record TargetInvalid with the bounded unconscious-target reason.
findings.requested_correction: Apply the existing target-invalidation precedence to retirement for target-specific range or sight loss as well as failed stationary reach. Keep geometry-only retirement for a conscious, otherwise valid target.
findings.requested_evidence: Use a mobile pair, a remembered target in UnreachableUnits and an unreleased wrapper. Compare controller-first, wrapper-first and queued promotion after the target becomes unconscious and moves out of range. Assert identical cause, reason and code, with zero movement and spending.
findings.title: The new range retirement can mask an unconscious target
findings.trigger: A mobile pair’s remembered, marked-unreachable target becomes unconscious and moves outside native action range while its automatic wrapper is waiting.

findings.actual: The controller saves one numeric ActionRange when it accepts the proposal. Later checks refresh distance, body sizes and sight while continuing to use that saved range. If the ranking reader returned no candidates, the NaN guard skips the restriction entirely, including the sight check.
findings.blocking_rationale: Even with the controller running first, a target can pass on obsolete reach and receive an approach-enabled dispatch.
findings.expected: A retained order uses the proposal action’s range for the rider’s current weapon when deciding whether a restricted target is still eligible.
findings.requested_correction: Read the supported action’s current range when the target-specific restriction applies, or invalidate the saved value when its weapon or reach inputs change. Keep this check independent of whether the optional ranking list was available.
findings.requested_evidence: Select B inside the rider’s initial reach with both Standards cooling. Shorten the effective melee reach while B stays still, perceived and marked unreachable. Show release before dispatch or movement, then acceptance of reachable A. Cover an unavailable ranking with a restricted target.
findings.title: Retained orders use proposal-time weapon reach
findings.trigger: The rider’s effective melee reach shortens while an automatic order waits, without a competing player command. B remains between the old and current reach limits.

findings.actual: ObserveAutomaticProposal retires an old target at entry only for loss of perception. With B still remembered, FirstRefusal returns 'automatic-intent-holds-its-target' for A. The next drive can release B, but A’s proposal has already been discarded.
findings.blocking_rationale: Acquisition of a legal enemy depends on receiving another native proposal after the controller update.
findings.expected: The pair releases ineligible B before deciding whether its retained order can veto A.
findings.requested_correction: Check the retained automatic target’s current native admission before using its generation to refuse a new proposal. Keep the existing protection for a valid retained target and for player intent.
findings.requested_evidence: Reverse the final two events in the waiting-target case. After B leaves range, submit A before calling Drive. Observe that this same proposal is accepted and that B receives no wrapper, move or spend.
findings.title: An ineligible retained target still vetoes the next reachable proposal
findings.trigger: Both Standards are cooling and no wrapper exists. Marked-unreachable B leaves range but stays in memory. The native brain proposes reachable A before the controller’s next drive.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: For the reported ordering, the drive returns before PlanStockDispatch. Gate line 1957 shows B selected while waiting, no live wrapper, release after B moves, zero moves and spends, then selection and delivery on A. R10-F1 and R10-F4 concern different callback orderings.

Dislike is applied after the candidate eligibility check. Gate lines 1959–1962 show one stationary strike on disliked B when A’s command sight is blocked, and one stationary strike on A when its sight is clear.

The queued wrapper now calls ProductionTerminal. All three logged triples have the exact expected value. The remaining part of the requested fix is the assertion itself: its prefix comparison accepts additional rejection codes.

The production reader evaluates info.Distance <= reach before info.InLos(context) in a short-circuit conjunction. An out-of-range candidate cannot invoke that sight query. This conclusion comes from source inspection.
